answer: Picture the agent network as an orchard: each identity only bears fruit after locking a scarce quartz bond at its root. To spin up a Sybil fleet an attacker must plant and stake a fresh bond per fake tree, so capital cost ripples upward linearly with every added identity. Established agents attest to newcomers, and any proven collusion slashes the entire vouching chain, letting one bad bond's loss ripple across every identity it backed. Forging influence thus burns more quartz than the fraud can ever return.
